messages:
Mira: Customer reports intermittent 401 "invalid_api_key" only for long prompts; short prompts are fine.

Mira: Repro they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<~8k tokens prompt here>"}]}'
```

Mira: Short prompt (~100 tokens) => 200 OK. Long prompt (~3k+ tokens) => 401 invalid_api_key, same key.

Jordan: Any request headers, content-length, or request id they can share?

Mira: They sent response with x-request-id: req_08f3b2c7 and backend log snippet: `auth: key_type=hosted, route=throughput, allowed=false`

Ashley: That log means routing sent the request to the "throughput" pool which requires dedicated-capable keys. We have a rule that routes by payload/sequence length to throughput for higher batch efficiency.

Mira: Customer is on hosted-only key (free tier). So short requests go to hosted cluster, long requests hit throughput pool -> 401 because key lacks permission.

Jordan: I can reproduce locally by setting Content-Length ~50k with a hosted key -> 401 with same req id pattern.

Mira: Asked customer to confirm key origin (dashboard hosted key). They confirmed.

Ashley: Mitigations:
- Split prompt into smaller chunks (workaround)
- Upgrade to Dedicated / obtain a dedicated-capable key
- Use our chunking service/pagination as temporary bypass (not ideal)

Mira: Filing internal doc update to clarify routing behavior by payload length and to improve error messaging (should surface 'upgrade required for large payloads' instead of generic 401).

Jordan: Filing bug INF-4789: "routing: large payloads rejected for hosted keys" -> owner: eng-runtime.

Ashley: Support playbook change: always check payload size + route logs when seeing auth 401 but key is valid.

Mira: @eng-runtime can the runtime team confirm whether we want a soft fallback to hosted pool or an explicit 403/upgrade guidance? :eyes:

eng-runtime-bot: Ticket created: INF-4789 "routing: large payloads rejected for hosted keys" assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

Mira: Closed loop w/ customer: explained cause, suggested chunking, opened upgrade path with sales. Customer accepted temporary chunking.
